title: Hook timeouts: a flat 30s is wrong in both directions, and the cap is doing telemetry's job

verdict.rationale: The issue is about the flat 30s hook timeout (defaultHookTimeoutSec) introduced in a Codex SessionEnd commit. The evidence covers local_dev removal, legacy hook prefix handling, and Factory AI Droid agent scaffolding, and none of it discusses hook timeouts. The blamed dropStaleEntireHooks code is only tangentially related, so there is no usable record for the timeout decision.

refactor(hooks)!: remove local_dev mode

Local-dev mode pointed installed hooks at `scripts/entire-dev`, a launcher
inside the working tree that compiled and ran the checked-out source. It was
read from the *committed* `.entire/settings.json` (settings.go merged
`local_dev` from the project scope, and strategy/common.go regenerated the git
hook from it), so any repository could commit `"local_dev": true` and have
`entire enable` install hooks that execute that repository's own code. A branch
checkout could then swap what ran. This repo shipped exactly that: `local_dev:
true` was tracked, and all six committed agent configs invoked the launcher.

Hooks now always name the `entire` binary. Removed the `--local-dev` flags
(including the non-hidden one on `entire agent add`), `EnableOptions.LocalDev`,
the `localDev` parameter from `Agent.InstallHooks` across all nine agents and
the external-agent protocol, the claude-code local-dev SessionEnd timeout, and
the launcher script.

`EntireSettings.LocalDev` stays as a documented no-op: the loaders use
DisallowUnknownFields, so deleting the field would make every existing settings
file containing `local_dev` a hard parse error. It is not merged from overrides
and nothing reads it, matching the `Strategy` precedent.

Removing the feature is not enough to disarm existing installs, so this also
fixes how hooks written by older versions get replaced:

- `isGitHookInstalledInHooksDir` only looked for the Entire marker, which a

refactor(hooks): make legacy hook prefixes unusable for writing

The detection list carried a comment saying the legacy shapes were lookup-only,
but nothing enforced it: `LegacyLocalDevHookScript` was exported, so any agent
could splice it into a generated hook command and only a reviewer would catch it.

The recognized set now lives unexported inside the agent package, and both
`IsManagedHookCommand` and `DropStaleManagedHooks` drop their `prefixes`
parameter. Production code cannot name a legacy shape, so it cannot install one
— attempting either route is a compile error rather than a convention violation.
Construction stays available to tests through agent/testutil, which is test-only
by definition.

This also removes the six per-agent `entireHookPrefixes` literals. Five were
byte-identical and claudecode differed only in resolving the repo root through
${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} rather than git; the shared set now covers all four shapes
Entire has ever written, matched for every agent. A hook naming any of them is
ours regardless of whose config it appears in, and a newly added agent inherits
legacy detection instead of having to remember to copy the list — omitting those
entries is exactly what leaves an old hook installed forever.

Every agent's current prefix was already the same bare "entire ", which is why
the parameter had no remaining purpose.
